requirements.requirement: Configure the opsadmin account on node1 with the specified SSH public key for SSH access.
requirements.summary: The account exists, its password is locked, the authorized_keys file has secure ownership and permissions, and the exact requested key remained present after restart. SSH was running and listening on port 22.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication by disabling password and keyboard-interactive authentication.
requirements.summary: The effective global and per-user sshd configuration enables public keys, disables password and keyboard-interactive methods, and requires AuthenticationMethods publickey. Live probes before and after restart were offered only publickey authentication.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is also complete: it recorded a healthy pre-restart state and acknowledgement, observed a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and demonstrated recovery of sshd, the listener, key-only policy, account, and exact key.
limitations: No successful end-to-end login using the private key corresponding to the installed public key was captured. Access is therefore established through exact key placement, permissions, effective sshd configuration, and service/listener health rather than a positive authentication test.
The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because it checked systemd on Alpine; direct OpenRC sshd status checks nevertheless showed the relevant service healthy.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account/key creation, password locking, permission hardening, sshd configuration and reload were directly related to the task; the reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol. Temporary-file and package-health inventories were unchanged, SSH remained the only TCP listener, and no abandoned artifacts or weakened controls were observed.
